newsitem.title: CHINA: China hit by drought in north, floods in south.
newsitem.headline: China hit by drought in north, floods in south.

text.p: Drought and high temperatures are plaguing northern China while floods are wreaking havoc in the south, posing threats to rice and other crops, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.

In the first ten days of July, temperatures in many areas in the north had risen by two to three degrees celsius, with rainfall dropping by as much as 50-90 percent from the same period last year to less than 20 millimetres, Xinhua said.
Much of northern China and parts of Inner Mongolia had seen less than 10 millimetres of rain in the period, a drop of 80-90 percent from the same time last year, the agency said.
The southeastern part of Shandong province had scarcely seen a drop of rain, it said without elaborating.
"High temperatures have exacerbated the development of the drought and seriously affected crop growth," it said but gave no details of which crops were affected.
Experts had forecast that about 30 millimetres of rain would fall in the second ten days of July, after which normal weather patterns would resume, it said.
Meanwhile, heavy rainfalls were threatening rice crops in areas south of the Yangtze River, it said.
Rainfall in much of the south was two to five times as much in the first ten days of July as during the same period last year, it said.
Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Guizhou and Guangdong provinces had all been hit by heavy rains, it said.
"Clouds and rain have meant little sunlight, which is not beneficial to the growth of early rice," it said.
